evidence_scope: Item 11 (docs/review_triage_20260918_1440.md): accuracy of LinearRaccess against Raccess Exact at w in {1,3,7,10,20,30,50}, on the 1,770 bpRNA sequences 300-1,000nt, testing whether raising the loop caps (to 60) is sufficient on its own, or whether beam width must also increase. Supports Discussion and Supplementary S4.

median_absolute_error_beam100_cap60_by_w.note: Decreases monotonically with w; this reflects P_u itself shrinking toward 0 as w grows (same effect as the w=1-vs-w>1 absolute-error split in Supplementary S1), not by itself evidence of good relative accuracy.

beam100_to_200_improvement_factor_by_w.note: Doubling the beam reduces median relative error far more than raising the cap alone did, but the improvement shrinks as w grows -- diminishing returns, not full convergence.

fraction_of_cells_with_p_exact_ge_0.01_b.note: The true (Raccess Exact) accessibility itself is rarely large at large w: 80.2% of cells reach P_u>=0.01 at w=1, versus 0.01% at w=50. Consistent with the mechanistic explanation: a long completely-unpaired run has low Boltzmann weight (fewer base pairs) in the true ensemble too, and beam pruning disproportionately drops the already-rare states needed to track it as w grows.

conclusion: Raising loop caps alone (100/60 vs 100/30) is not enough to make LinearRaccess accurate at w approaching or exceeding the default cap; beam width is the binding constraint, and doubling it (100->200) cuts median relative error 3- to 31-fold depending on w. LinearRaccess remains substantially more accurate than Raccess Window at every tested w regardless of beam setting.
